body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. Gunfire near El Encanto Court in central Bakersfield just after 1 a.m. tops a night that also brought two foot chases, several weapons calls, and a pair of small fires. Today looks warm and breezy — a high near 84 under a Lake Wind Advisory — with air quality at 111, unhealthy for sensitive groups. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The loudest call of the night came at 1:09 a.m., when multiple callers reported gunshots near El Encanto Court in central Bakersfield. Officers responded to the area; no further details were available by morning.

Weapons calls ran on either side of midnight. At 7:26 p.m., officers were sent to Rench Road in north Bakersfield, where a teenager was reported to be holding a knife in the living room of a home while his parents were present. It wasn't clear whether he had brandished it or made any threats. Just after midnight, at 12:02 a.m., deputies headed to the 11,500 block of Old River Road in southwest Bakersfield, where a person was reported to be brandishing a knife at a group gathered around a gold pickup, and one person reported an assault.

Domestic violence calls carried the early morning hours. At 4:56 a.m., a woman told dispatchers she was being abused by her child's father, then disconnected; an infant could be heard crying in the background. Deputies were sent at 5:53 a.m. to a disturbance where a man was reported to have pinned his mother against a wall during an argument involving a juvenile. A court order was already in place in that case.

Two foot chases ended in arrests. At 10:19 p.m., officers chased a man who ran from a suspicious person call at a storage yard on the 4,000 block of Chester Avenue, reaching toward his waistband as he ran. He climbed onto a roof on the 3,300 block of Anderson Street, and with Air 1 overhead and a K-9 in place, he came down and was taken into custody, with resisting charges added. A second chase at 11:40 p.m. ended on Sky Ranch, where a driver and a passenger were arrested at a residence on Suncrest Drive; one person was still outstanding.

Fire crews stayed busy too. A vegetation fire of about three and a half acres was worked off Washington Street at 7:22 p.m., and crews responded to a fire on westbound Highway 58 just west of the Mount Vernon Avenue exit at 9:06 p.m., where a second ambulance was requested.

## Today's weather

It's 54 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 84 and a low around 54 tonight. The National Weather Service in Hanford has a Lake Wind Advisory in effect until 10 a.m. Saturday, so expect gusty conditions around the lake and open stretches of the valley. Air quality is 111 — unhealthy for sensitive groups — so folks with heart or lung conditions may want to keep outdoor time short this afternoon. No active fires were reported as of this morning.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned amid affair scandals.** The story is developing, and full details weren't immediately available; we'll pass along more as it comes. Nvidia has become one of the most closely watched companies in the country, and any leadership change at the top draws attention well beyond the tech world.

**According to 23ABC, community colleges are rushing to expand semiconductor training as the U.S. chip industry faces a labor shortage.** The station profiled students in short, hands-on chip-manufacturing courses — including a 23-year-old who took on more than $100,000 in debt for a business degree before signing up for a tuition-free, three-month program in Arizona that put him in a lab operating the machinery that turns silicon into chips. His cohort includes a 64-year-old middle school teacher, a laid-off software developer in his 50s, and gig workers without degrees. The goal is to fill entry-level technician jobs quickly as major chipmakers struggle to staff new U.S. plants.

**23ABC also sat down with the mother of Angel De Jesus Lucio, the Kern County soldier killed in Iraq, 20 years after his death.** Lucio, an Army sergeant, enlisted in August 2002 and died on Nov. 11, 2006, at age 22, alongside two other soldiers on a security escort mission in Ar Ramadi. His mother, Marina Lucio, told the station through an interpreter that Veterans Day brings mixed emotions — sadness, and happy memories of his childhood and the way he looked after his four younger brothers. The family visits the cemetery each year to pay their respects.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Movember experts are urging men to speak up and seek care earlier.** The annual campaign puts a spotlight on men's health through November, and the message this year is straightforward: don't wait on symptoms or screenings. We'll have more on local resources as the month goes on.

**California families are calling for changes to the state's juvenile justice system, 23ABC reports.** At a recent press conference, families who lost loved ones to violence involving juveniles joined district attorneys in arguing that current law limits accountability. Monterey County District Attorney Jeannine Pacioni said victims face the reality that a person responsible for even a murder may return to the community within a few years. Clovis father Stephen Quick, whose son Caleb was shot in 2025 in a case involving two juvenile suspects, said he is still far from justice after a judge found one suspect guilty but rehabilitatable. The families point to Proposition 57, which ended direct filing by prosecutors, and Senate Bill 1391, which prevents 14- and 15-year-olds from being transferred to adult court — laws whose effects have been felt here in Bakersfield.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski and the Yankees' Cam Schlittler were unanimous selections as Cy Young winners.** The honors cap the season for two of the game's rising arms.

## Something good

Bakersfield marked Veterans Day with its 107th annual parade, a tradition that once again brought neighbors out along the route to honor local service members. The American Legion also hosted a free breakfast and lunch for veterans in Bakersfield as part of the day's observances — a simple, generous way to say thank you to the people who served. If you know a veteran who couldn't make it out, a call this week still counts for plenty.

## Coming up this week

The Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee meets Friday, Nov. 13, at noon — a good one for anyone interested in local cleanup and beautification efforts. On Saturday, Nov. 13, the Fox Theater hosts NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet, an early start to the holiday season downtown.

Next week fills up quickly. The Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 2 p.m., and the Historic Preservation Commission meets that same day at 4 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, brings two City Council sessions at 515 — one at 3:30 p.m. and the regular meeting at 5:15 p.m. The Planning Commission meets Thursday, Nov. 19, at 5:30 p.m.

Also on the calendar: The 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards at the Fox Theater on Sunday, Nov. 15 — a milestone night for the local music community. Looking further out, the Fox has Cults & Classics: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? on Nov. 23, Becky Robinson's Holiday Spectacular on Nov. 27, and the Shrek Rave holiday edition on Dec. 4.

Have a good Thursday, and keep an eye on the wind if you're headed out to the lake.

top.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid affair scandals
